response.reason: Eight NL segments describe a microwave control state machine with states DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking. I extracted: initial entry to DoorShut; self-loop/retention on DoorShut under Cancel; transition endpoints DoorShut<->DoorOpen with event Door Opened/door closed; DoorOpen<->DoorOpenWithItem; DoorOpenWithItem->DoorShutWithItem and ->ReadytoCook with guards; DoorShutWithItem<->DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem->ReadytoCook with display/update effect; ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem with cancel/update effect, ReadytoCook->DoorOpenWithItem; ReadytoCook->Cooking with timer start action; Cooking->DoorOpenWithItem with timer stop action, Cooking->DoorShutWithItem on timer expiry, Cooking->ReadytoCook on Cancel. No explicit containment hierarchy beyond a flat state set, no explicit cardinality/region claims, no explicit termination state (all transitions cycle), so no termination contracts were created. State-action contracts were created for timer start/stop as explicit control actions tied to entry/exit-like phases, and display/update of cooking time as effect/variable-delta contracts. event_consumer_coverage was not separately warranted since no segment states an event must be accepted across a broader scope beyond the local transition. Each transition group captures shared source with alternatives and event/guard projections; guard_disjointness added for groups with genuinely distinguishable guarded alternatives (NL1 Cancel-retain vs door-opened-transition from DoorShut; NL4 alternatives from DoorOpenWithItem).

arguments.reason: Eight NL segments describe a microwave control state machine with states DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking. I extracted: initial entry to DoorShut; self-loop/retention on DoorShut under Cancel; transition endpoints DoorShut<->DoorOpen with event Door Opened/door closed; DoorOpen<->DoorOpenWithItem; DoorOpenWithItem->DoorShutWithItem and ->ReadytoCook with guards; DoorShutWithItem<->DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem->ReadytoCook with display/update effect; ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem with cancel/update effect, ReadytoCook->DoorOpenWithItem; ReadytoCook->Cooking with timer start action; Cooking->DoorOpenWithItem with timer stop action, Cooking->DoorShutWithItem on timer expiry, Cooking->ReadytoCook on Cancel. No explicit containment hierarchy beyond a flat state set, no explicit cardinality/region claims, no explicit termination state (all transitions cycle), so no termination contracts were created. State-action contracts were created for timer start/stop as explicit control actions tied to entry/exit-like phases, and display/update of cooking time as effect/variable-delta contracts. event_consumer_coverage was not separately warranted since no segment states an event must be accepted across a broader scope beyond the local transition. Each transition group captures shared source with alternatives and event/guard projections; guard_disjointness added for groups with genuinely distinguishable guarded alternatives (NL1 Cancel-retain vs door-opened-transition from DoorShut; NL4 alternatives from DoorOpenWithItem).

Defines DoorShutWithItem alternatives to DoorOpenWithItem and ReadytoCook, plus display/update effect at ReadytoCook.
Defines ReadytoCook alternatives to DoorShutWithItem (with cancel/update effect) and DoorOpenWithItem.
Defines ReadytoCook->Cooking on Start action, with timer-start action at Cooking entry.
Defines Cooking alternatives to DoorOpenWithItem (with timer stop action), DoorShutWithItem on timer expiry, and ReadytoCook on Cancel.

result.reason: Eight NL segments describe a microwave control state machine with states DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking. I extracted: initial entry to DoorShut; self-loop/retention on DoorShut under Cancel; transition endpoints DoorShut<->DoorOpen with event Door Opened/door closed; DoorOpen<->DoorOpenWithItem; DoorOpenWithItem->DoorShutWithItem and ->ReadytoCook with guards; DoorShutWithItem<->DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem->ReadytoCook with display/update effect; ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem with cancel/update effect, ReadytoCook->DoorOpenWithItem; ReadytoCook->Cooking with timer start action; Cooking->DoorOpenWithItem with timer stop action, Cooking->DoorShutWithItem on timer expiry, Cooking->ReadytoCook on Cancel. No explicit containment hierarchy beyond a flat state set, no explicit cardinality/region claims, no explicit termination state (all transitions cycle), so no termination contracts were created. State-action contracts were created for timer start/stop as explicit control actions tied to entry/exit-like phases, and display/update of cooking time as effect/variable-delta contracts. event_consumer_coverage was not separately warranted since no segment states an event must be accepted across a broader scope beyond the local transition. Each transition group captures shared source with alternatives and event/guard projections; guard_disjointness added for groups with genuinely distinguishable guarded alternatives (NL1 Cancel-retain vs door-opened-transition from DoorShut; NL4 alternatives from DoorOpenWithItem).

All endpoint contracts (NL1-INIT-1 through NL8-ENDPOINT-3) have exact matching edges in inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions with correct source/target/trigger, so no S2 candidates are raised for those. The event_consumer_coverage derived contract (Cancel in DoorShut) is satisfied because Cancel is consumed at DoorShut (transition:line:17), ReadytoCook (line:26), and Cooking (line:31), all reachable_from_initial=true; declared and reachable consumer sets are identical for every event in the model, so no coverage gap exists anywhere. No termination_state contract exists (final_states=[] and no NL8 contract declares state_role=termination_state), so no termination candidate is derivable. No deadlock/dead-end frontier fact exists: every state has outgoing_transition_refs, metrics.unreachable_state_count=0, and verify_facts proves reachability for every state with no non_proved entries; thus no V1 or G1 candidate is warranted. The guard_disjointness contract (NL4-DISJOINT-1) is omitted since the two DoorOpenWithItem alternatives fire on distinct triggers (Door_Closed vs Cooking_Time_Entered), which operationally distinguishes them despite the NL phrasing describing guards. Effect/action/variable-delta contracts (NL5-EFFECT-1, NL6-EFFECT-1, NL7-ACTION-1, NL8-ACTION-1, and the two DERIVED variable_delta contracts) show every relevant FCSTM transition/state parsed with empty effects/actions arrays (see inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions[].effects=[] for tr on lines 23,25,26,28,29,30 and states have no action fields), which is a precise behavioral gap: the closed model carries no explicit action/effect despite explicit NL obligation, warranting predicate-null W1 candidates bound to the exact carrier refs.

Three independently violable obligations were omitted: (1) NL1's explicit Cancel-action effect in DoorShut establishes an event-consumer-coverage obligation distinct from the state_retention contract already present, since consumption and retention are separate typed properties; (2) NL5 explicitly requires both display and update of cooking time, and the update component is an independently violable variable_delta obligation on the named data subject beyond the general effect contract; (3) NL6 explicitly requires canceling or updating cooking time on the Cancel transition, which is a variable_delta obligation on the same data subject separate from the effect-carrier contract already present. contract_extraction.reason: Eight NL segments describe a microwave control state machine with states DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking. I extracted: initial entry to DoorShut; self-loop/retention on DoorShut under Cancel; transition endpoints DoorShut<->DoorOpen with event Door Opened/door closed; DoorOpen<->DoorOpenWithItem; DoorOpenWithItem->DoorShutWithItem and ->ReadytoCook with guards; DoorShutWithItem<->DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem->ReadytoCook with display/update effect; ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem with cancel/update effect, ReadytoCook->DoorOpenWithItem; ReadytoCook->Cooking with timer start action; Cooking->DoorOpenWithItem with timer stop action, Cooking->DoorShutWithItem on timer expiry, Cooking->ReadytoCook on Cancel. No explicit containment hierarchy beyond a flat state set, no explicit cardinality/region claims, no explicit termination state (all transitions cycle), so no termination contracts were created. State-action contracts were created for timer start/stop as explicit control actions tied to entry/exit-like phases, and display/update of cooking time as effect/variable-delta contracts. event_consumer_coverage was not separately warranted since no segment states an event must be accepted across a broader scope beyond the local transition. Each transition group captures shared source with alternatives and event/guard projections; guard_disjointness added for groups with genuinely distinguishable guarded alternatives (NL1 Cancel-retain vs door-opened-transition from DoorShut; NL4 alternatives from DoorOpenWithItem).

All endpoint contracts (NL1-NL8) are satisfied by exact transitions with matching source/target/trigger. The initial entry [*] -> DoorShut is present and owned by the root machine, satisfying NL1-INIT-1. The retention self-loop DoorShut->DoorShut on Cancel exists (transition:line:17), satisfying NL1-RETAIN-1 and the derived event-consumer-coverage contract (Cancel is reachably consumed at DoorShut, ReadytoCook, Cooking). The guard-disjointness contract NL4-DISJOINT-1 cannot be resolved by any frozen predicate (guard_disjointness has none) and the closed model shows both DoorOpenWithItem outgoing alternatives (tr to DoorShutWithItem on Door_Closed, tr to ReadytoCook on Cooking_Time_Entered) use distinct triggers, not guards, so no observable ambiguity is evidenced; since NL explicitly requires distinguishability and the FCSTM realizes the two alternatives via distinct discrete events (not overlapping guards), I omit this contract as satisfied rather than manufacturing a false candidate, because the discrete-event triggers already make the alternatives distinguishable in the closed model. stage_receipts.reason: Eight NL segments describe a microwave control state machine with states DoorShut, DoorOpen, DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem, ReadytoCook, Cooking. I extracted: initial entry to DoorShut; self-loop/retention on DoorShut under Cancel; transition endpoints DoorShut<->DoorOpen with event Door Opened/door closed; DoorOpen<->DoorOpenWithItem; DoorOpenWithItem->DoorShutWithItem and ->ReadytoCook with guards; DoorShutWithItem<->DoorOpenWithItem, DoorShutWithItem->ReadytoCook with display/update effect; ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem with cancel/update effect, ReadytoCook->DoorOpenWithItem; ReadytoCook->Cooking with timer start action; Cooking->DoorOpenWithItem with timer stop action, Cooking->DoorShutWithItem on timer expiry, Cooking->ReadytoCook on Cancel. No explicit containment hierarchy beyond a flat state set, no explicit cardinality/region claims, no explicit termination state (all transitions cycle), so no termination contracts were created. State-action contracts were created for timer start/stop as explicit control actions tied to entry/exit-like phases, and display/update of cooking time as effect/variable-delta contracts. event_consumer_coverage was not separately warranted since no segment states an event must be accepted across a broader scope beyond the local transition. Each transition group captures shared source with alternatives and event/guard projections; guard_disjointness added for groups with genuinely distinguishable guarded alternatives (NL1 Cancel-retain vs door-opened-transition from DoorShut; NL4 alternatives from DoorOpenWithItem).
